headline: Chip-led selloff and AI jitters test nerves as earnings open
body: The dominant story this morning is a semiconductor-led selloff that started in Asia and is bleeding into Western markets. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell sharply overnight, dragging a broad Asian benchmark to its lowest level since August, and the pressure is carrying into US futures, which are mixed rather than uniformly weak -- the Dow leaning modestly firmer while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq lean slightly negative. Europe is the outlier, with the Stoxx 600 edging higher as falling oil prices and softer bond yields lift rate-sensitive, economically exposed shares. That split -- chip-heavy indexes under pressure, broader cyclical markets steadier -- reads more like a sector-specific wobble than a broad flight from risk, at least for now.

Layered on top of the hardware selloff is a renewed round of unease about AI-sector spending and valuations, the kind of 'is this a bubble' chatter that has resurfaced periodically this year without fully resolving either way. That backdrop meets a fresh catalyst today as big US bank earnings season opens, with JPMorgan among the first to report and more large banks due through the week -- a results season that will either steady nerves or add to them depending on what management teams say about credit, rates, and the broader spending outlook. Retail chatter on today's news flow was thin in what we could find, so this read leans more on price action and headline-driven positioning than on any clear social-sentiment signal.
